answer: Proof of work alone fails for agents because one operator can spin up thousands of identities for almost nothing. A stronger filter is stake that gets locked for a long time and slashed when an identity is caught colluding. Peers can also grade each other on tasks that only a real, independent agent would finish, then cross-check those grades against a mirror of the grading history. Identities that always vouch for the same cluster stand out quickly, like a single dune of sand standing apart from the mesa around it.
